source.title: Is GPT-OSS Good? A Comprehensive Evaluation of OpenAI's Latest Open Source Models
source.authors: Zi-Qian Bi; Ke-Yu Chen; Chiung-Yi Tseng; Danyang Zhang; Tian-Yang Wang; Hong-Ying Luo; Lu Chen; Jun-Min Huang; Jibin Guan; Junfeng Hao; Jun-Jie Song

record.file_problem: None; the full paper text is present. The paper contains conflicting benchmark scores in its prose and Table II.
record.tranche_reason: It compares benchmark accuracy across differently sized models, a different measure and setup from pretraining-loss scaling, and reports results relevant to downstream predictability (V6).
record.gate_note: The study evaluates downstream benchmark accuracy, not held-out pretraining cross-entropy. It does not sweep training tokens or compute, fit or extrapolate loss power laws, or compare parameter/token allocations at a fixed compute budget. Its benchmark comparisons are relevant to V6, but not to V1–V5 or V7. Chain-of-thought gains are prompted interventions and are not evidence of naturally arising scale effects. Table II and the prose report conflicting scores for several benchmarks; both are recorded separately below.
record.test_reason: It compares downstream benchmark accuracy of two released sparse MoE GPT-OSS models (21B/3.6B active vs 117B/5.1B active), framed as a test of scaling expectations. That bears weakly on V6 in a new MoE setting. It is only two points, and training data, tokens and recipe are not controlled. It has no loss, token or compute sweeps, so V1–V5 and V7 are untested.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely right. Specifically, the authors report that gpt-oss-20B matches or beats gpt-oss-120B on about half of the benchmarks (MMLU, SciQ, ties on MedQA and DialogSum), while 120B wins elsewhere. They attribute this to MoE routing or training inefficiencies and conclude that parameter count alone does not predict capability. They also recommend 20B for cost-performance (5x less memory, 2.6x less energy per response). Their claim that 120B 'consistently underperforms' overstates their own numbers.
record.recipe_differences: Downstream benchmark evaluation of existing models rather than pretraining-loss scaling sweeps, loss-law fitting, extrapolation, or fixed-compute allocation experiments.
record.method_sensitivity: Benchmark/task changes the direction and magnitude of the 20B–120B comparison. The paper reports conflicting scores for multiple benchmarks between its prose and Table II.
record.code_released: not stated (the paper refers to a Project Webpage but gives no URL in the text)
record.problems: No held-out pretraining-loss measurements, controlled training-size/token/compute sweep, loss-law fit, or compute-optimal allocation analysis. Comparisons involve different released models and do not isolate parameter count from training and architecture. The paper reports contradictory benchmark scores in prose and Table II; reported statistical-test and confidence-interval claims are not attached to the individual scores recorded here.
record.rows_left_out: No additional score rows were retained for other models, aggregate rankings, figures, or efficiency measures: they do not add a controlled GPT-OSS size comparison for V6 beyond the reported paired benchmark results. Prompted chain-of-thought gain figures were omitted because they measure an induced prompting intervention, not performance arising from scale alone.

untested.parts: All: no pretraining loss and no parameter, token or compute sweep.
All: no fitted law and no extrapolation.
All: no controlled shape variation at fixed parameter count.
All: no other modality or regime fitted.
Prediction from pretraining loss; a quantitative trend over more than two sizes; scale-controlled comparisons with the same data and recipe.
All: no exponents or fitting choices.

missing.what: The results overview gives MMLU as 69% vs 64%, while V-B, Fig 7 and V-K give 69% vs 66%.

record.verdict_notes: This is weak evidence for V6. It rests on only two released models, whose active parameters differ by only 1.4x (3.6B vs 5.1B) and whose training data and recipe are uncontrolled. Table II explicitly averages the study's results with published results. Its GPT-OSS values differ from the study's own Fig 7 and prose, and show an implausibly uniform 3-point gap, so Table II rows are set to cannot_determine and given no verdict. The reader's apparent SciQ prose conflict is a misreading of V-A: all passages put 20B at 87% and 120B at 82%. The reported statistics are internally inconsistent: it claims p<0.05 for all differences including ties, and cites both Benjamini-Hochberg and Bonferroni corrections. The tranche was changed from T2 to T3 (a sparse-MoE setting with downstream benchmarks only).

versions.untested_parts: Held-out pretraining loss versus parameters, tokens, or compute; several orders of magnitude and non-bottleneck conditions.
Fitting on small runs and predicting much larger runs.
Loss-minimising parameter/token allocation at fixed compute and its trend with compute.
Controlled comparisons of architecture details at fixed parameter count.
Power laws in other modalities or training regimes.
The study measures downstream benchmark accuracy, not prediction from pretraining loss; it does not establish a general quantitative predictive law.
Fitted exponents, fitting choices, compute-optimal allocation, and curvature of fitted loss curves.

relationships.condition: GPT-OSS 20B vs 120B, study's own scores (prose/Fig 7) on GSM8K, HumanEval, FinQA, PIQA, LegalQA
relationships.reason: The larger variant scores higher on all five (e.g. 87 vs 73 HumanEval, 84 vs 58 FinQA): rows P-GSM8K-*, P-HE-*, P-FinQA-*, P-PIQA-*, P-LegalQA-*.
relationships.display_finding: The larger variant scored higher on all five benchmarks, including 87 versus 73 on HumanEval and 84 versus 58 on FinQA.

relationships.condition: GPT-OSS 20B vs 120B, study's own scores on MMLU, SciQ, C-Eval (reversed) and MedQA, DialogSum (flat)
relationships.reason: The smaller model wins on MMLU (69 vs 66), SciQ (87 vs 82) and C-Eval (28 vs 20, near chance), and ties at 82 and 88 on MedQA and DialogSum: rows P-MMLU-*, P-SciQ-*, P-CEval-*, P-MedQA-*, P-DialogSum-*.
relationships.display_finding: The 20B model beat 120B on MMLU at 69 versus 66, SciQ at 87 versus 82 and C-Eval at 28 versus 20, while tying at 82 on MedQA and 88 on DialogSum.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
